heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for professional visual content creation across images, edits, and video generation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a bold editorial hero with a bright white canvas and an expansive mesh-gradient field behind layered product previews. Keep the main copy left-aligned, but place the visual system as an asymmetrical floating composition across the center-right so the hero does not feel like a standard split layout. blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore ByteDance generative models for premium AI image and video creation. Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro help creative teams generate high-quality visuals, cinematic motion, and synchronized audio-video output.

sections.backgroundTreatment: editorial white base with precision-line overlays and floating preview tiles
sections.designNote: Use a content-first split hero that answers the three required questions clearly: headline states the product category, subheadline names creative teams as the audience, and the CTA is the only action. Right side should show layered product visuals: image output frames, short video timeline strips, waveform accents, and small proof chips. Keep the headline compact and premium; avoid a generic SaaS illustration.

Place recognisable customer/partner logos immediately after the hero in a calm horizontal flex-wrap grid. If real logos are unavailable or too weak, replace with a restrained metric strip. This should be the first trust signal and visually quieter than the hero, using white cards and subtle borders.

Create two distinct product blocks with alternating rhythm. First block: Seedream 4.5 as a spotlight panel with a large visual preview on one side and a compact feature stack on the other, emphasizing text-to-image, editing, composition, typography, and 1K–4K fidelity. Second block: Seedance 1.5 Pro in a different visual language, using an accordion-with-visual workflow that highlights text-to-video, synchronized audio-video generation, lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and faster inference. Do not use a flat static card grid for the five-plus features.

If kept, treat this as a utility credibility block rather than a marketing section. Use a simple icon-list or short card grid focused on buying confidence, demo support, and enterprise readiness. Keep it tighter and less expressive than the product blocks.

Present pricing as two strong comparison cards, with Seedance 1.5 Pro visually emphasized because it has an explicit starting price. Keep CTAs consistent as 'Get started' on every button, but in the pricing area the button should read as a quote/request action visually while still using the required CTA label. Use one highlighted card and one secondary card, not a dense pricing table.

Use a three-card testimonial grid with editorial quote styling and compact attribution. Focus the first two quotes on creative outcomes and the third on evaluation/demo ease. Keep this section visually lighter than pricing and more human than the product module.

End with a focused conversion block that feels like the natural next step after proof. Use a centered floating card with strong whitespace, a concise prompt, and one full-width mobile CTA. Keep the CTA visually dominant in accent orange at full opacity. This is the final and strongest conversion moment.
Omit a moving media strip unless real media logos are available. Do not use marquee behavior. If needed, keep a tiny static footer trust row only.

blueprint.designPersonality: Editorial, intelligent, and production-grade. Clean white canvases, crisp orange accents, soft shadows, and structured spacing make the page feel premium and trustworthy for enterprise creative teams. The tone should communicate powerful generative capability with control, quality, and speed.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use polished product-style visual composition rather than people photography: abstract AI output frames, typography-rich image mockups, video storyboard strips, audio waveform accents, and floating proof badges. Include a dominant logo trust band near the top using SVG logos, since logos are the primary trust signal. The hero should feel like a creative production desk with layered outputs and precision UI, not a neon AI fantasy.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so it needs a compact size to preserve hierarchy and prevent line breaks from overpowering the hero layout.

colours.colourReason: Brand colors are locked to Techjockey’s provided palette. White becomes the hero base for an editorial feel, while the brand orange drives CTAs, highlights, and progress accents. This keeps the page visually distinct without inventing a new palette.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen split hero with brand/logo anchoring, large left-aligned headline, short supporting copy, and a compact benefit list; primary CTA emphasis is deferred to the form section rather than the hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Top hero band followed by a conversion form block, then product feature sections stacked vertically with strong hierarchy and repeated headline-description-feature grouping; minimal lateral complexity, mostly one-column narrative flow after the hero.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple content cards with restrained styling, clear title/body separation, and utility-focused presentation; if used, cards should feel functional rather than decorative, with high readability and minimal chrome.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion CTA appears as a prominent form-driven action in a dedicated lead-gen block; secondary CTA usage is minimal or absent. Prefer one dominant action per section and avoid competing buttons.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern is present; omit pricing modules unless added separately as a dedicated conversion section.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not visible in the reference; use a lightweight, low-friction footer with minimal links and no heavy promotional content.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Hero uses logo/brand imagery only; no prominent product media, video, or gallery treatment is shown. Prefer restrained media placement and avoid large decorative visuals.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Section blocks follow a repeated structure: label/kicker, headline, explanatory paragraph, then a list of capability points. Each section reads like a feature module with progressive disclosure from summary to details.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form in its own card-like block with a clear heading, stacked fields, and hidden tracking inputs. Form is positioned as a separate conversion milestone immediately after the hero.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-first presentation with no apparent motion system; if motion is added, keep it subtle and functional, limited to basic hover/focus states and simple reveal transitions.
componentPatterns: feature list with repeated title-description rows
designNotes: Use a conversion-first layout that moves quickly from value proposition to form capture.
Keep hierarchy strong: logo, headline, short proof/value line, then supporting bullets.
Favor dense but readable content blocks over visual storytelling.
Use ample whitespace within sections, but avoid elaborate surface treatments.
Maintain consistent spacing and repeated section structure for long-form content.
If adding richer interactions later, preserve the simple enterprise/lead-gen tone.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for professionals evaluating advanced AI image and video models, so the structure should feel product-led, credible, and conversion-focused. Because the page goal is lead generation and the audience is solution-aware rather than cold, the design should quickly establish capability, then move into a dedicated conversion moment and supporting proof. The strongest trust signal is logos, so the visual system should prioritize logo-led validation, with testimonials as secondary reinforcement. A split hero works best for clear messaging without wasting space, while the rest of the page should use a balanced, vertically stacked rhythm to explain the two products cleanly and avoid confusion. CTA intensity should be medium: prominent enough to drive demos/quotes, but not so aggressive that it feels consumer-like or interrupts the premium, enterprise-oriented tone.
